docs.text: Parcelly refunds are issued to the original payment method within five business days. Customers can request a refund from the billing page for up to thirty days after a charge. Annual plans are refunded on a prorated basis, which means the unused months are returned and the used months are kept. Refunds for add-ons such as extra storage are processed together with the main plan. If the card was closed, the refund goes to the account balance as credit.

Invoices are generated on the first day of each billing cycle and sent by email to the billing contact. Each invoice lists the plan, the number of seats, taxes and any usage charges. Administrators can download past invoices as PDF files from the billing page. To add a company tax number or a purchase order reference, edit the billing profile before the next cycle starts. Changes do not apply to invoices that were already issued.

Single sign-on is available on the Business plan using SAML 2.0. Administrators upload the identity provider metadata file, map the email attribute and test the connection with one pilot user. After the test succeeds, enforcement can be turned on for the whole workspace. Members who signed up with a password keep access until enforcement is enabled. Service accounts are not covered by single sign-on and keep using API tokens.

The public API allows 600 requests per minute for each token. When the limit is passed, the server answers with status 429 and a Retry-After header that gives the number of seconds to wait. Clients should back off with an exponential delay and add random jitter. Bulk endpoints count as one request but accept up to one hundred items. Enterprise customers can ask support for a higher quota.

Webhooks send a signed JSON message to your server when a shipment changes state. Every delivery includes a signature header computed with HMAC and your signing secret. Verify the signature before you trust the body. If your server returns an error, Parcelly retries the delivery up to eight times over about one day, with longer pauses each time. Because retries can repeat an event, handlers should be idempotent and use the event id to skip duplicates.

Each shipment gets a tracking page with a public link that can be shared with the recipient. The page shows scans from the carrier, the estimated delivery window and any exception such as a failed attempt or an address problem. Tracking data is refreshed every fifteen minutes. Recipients can leave delivery instructions, for example a safe place or a neighbor, until the parcel is out for delivery.

Address validation checks a destination before a label is bought. It corrects the postal code format, flags missing apartment numbers and warns when the carrier does not deliver to a post office box. Results are marked as valid, corrected or invalid. Labels for invalid addresses are blocked by default, but an administrator can switch the policy to warn only. Validation covers over sixty countries.

The returns portal lets a recipient print a prepaid return label without contacting the sender. Senders choose which items can be returned and for how many days. When the carrier scans the return label, the shipment status changes to return in transit and the sender receives a notification. Return labels use the cheapest carrier service by default, and senders may pick a faster option.

Rate shopping compares the price and transit time of every connected carrier for a given parcel. You can sort quotes by cost or by speed and set rules, for example always choose the cheapest option under three days. Negotiated rates from your own carrier accounts are shown next to the discounted rates that Parcelly provides. Dimensional weight is calculated automatically from the box size.

Workspace members have one of four roles: owner, admin, member or viewer. Owners can change the plan and delete the workspace. Admins manage users, integrations and billing. Members create shipments and print labels. Viewers can only read shipment data and reports. Role changes take effect immediately and are recorded in the audit log, which owners can export as CSV.

Shipment records are kept for twenty-four months after delivery and then deleted. Label images are deleted after ninety days. Workspace owners can request an early deletion of personal data about a recipient by sending the recipient email address to the privacy contact. Deletion requests are completed within thirty days, and backups are overwritten on the normal schedule.

Parcelly connects to online shops through native plugins and through a generic CSV import. A plugin pulls new orders every five minutes, creates shipments and writes the tracking number back to the order. If an order is edited after the label was bought, the plugin does not change the label and shows a warning. The CSV import accepts a template with columns for name, address, weight and reference.

Service status and past incidents are published on the status page. Subscribers receive an email or a text message when an incident starts, when it is updated and when it is resolved. Planned maintenance is announced at least forty-eight hours ahead. After a major incident the team publishes a written review within five business days that explains the cause and the fixes.
